currentGap: The latest furniture and staging pass wins the blind comparison with the previous build. The Room 4 still wins the fixed comparison. The next pass targets contact grounding, localized light and physical material depth.

rounds.label: BASELINE
rounds.title: The existing physical room
rounds.summary: The working autonomous engine is retained. The initial visual review found a primitive room, a tiny probe, flat mechanisms and weak focal lighting.
rounds.gap: Crafted architecture, a developed protagonist and tactile mechanisms.

rounds.label: ITERATION 01
rounds.title: The archive takes shape
rounds.summary: A furnished archive, physical materials, an articulated archivist and a game-focused interface are now rendered. An independent critic inspected the actual captures.
rounds.gap: The central lock still reads as a ring on a blank door. Repetitive shiny wood and limited shadowing remain visible.

rounds.label: ITERATION 02
rounds.title: Physical mechanisms and a real escape
rounds.summary: All eight mechanism families now contain moving parts; the vault opens onto a passage. Real screenshots received another independent comparison with the fixed commercial reference.
rounds.gap: Nested rings still dominate the hero lock; character close-up was clipped, and portrait room framing was too distant. These findings are driving the next iteration.

rounds.label: ITERATION 03
rounds.title: Crafted vault, developed Archivist
rounds.summary: The vault now has meshing gears, connected drawbars and guided bolts. A complete character portrait, stronger portrait scene framing, furniture detail and a real exit passage are captured from the running renderer. A fresh chronology-blinded A/B critic preferred this build over baseline in every view and accepted the developed character; the separate commercial benchmark still wins.
rounds.gap: Repeated furniture silhouettes and staging, a clipped overview character, and the hard hover cone remain visible.

rounds.label: ITERATION 04
rounds.title: Constructed furniture and complete staging
rounds.summary: A shaped writing bench, upholstered chair, differentiated instrument stands and bookcase crowns are now visible. The overview keeps the whole Archivist in frame; confirmed escape stages the character at the open doorway. A fresh blind critic preferred this pass in four views, with the unchanged mechanism tied.
rounds.gap: Broad fill light, weak contact grounding and repeated wood/gold surface treatment still fall behind the fixed commercial reference.

checks: TypeScript build passed; 67 Escape Room unit and contract tests passed at the Round 04 checkpoint.
The real autonomous capture run escaped at tick 25 with all eight puzzles solved; no browser console/page errors were captured.
Nine independent browser scenarios passed at Round 03. The four-theme resource stress test passed separately on Round 04 with all 65 real renderer frames and unchanged assertions.
Five theme/replay cycles retained exactly 158 WebGL geometries, 21 textures and 13 shader programs. A separate raw-buffer regression held 348 outstanding buffers across six cycles.
Renderer teardown stops callbacks, removes listeners and retires its context while preserving shared assets used by a surviving renderer.
The existing desktop broadcast check failed its fixed 700 ms tick-change assertion before reaching rendering budget assertions; the failure is retained for investigation.
The Round 04 low-tier stills measured 170 draw calls / 111,128 triangles for the opening room and 180 / 113,612 for confirmed escape. These are capture measurements, not native-GPU performance proof.
Commercial comparisons remain unblinded; visual parity has not been established. Independent chronology-blinded comparisons prefer the new builds over their predecessors.
Character mesh submissions reduced from 61 to 39 with all 12,526 triangles and articulation retained.
Stream self-test passed: deterministic authority, public privacy, recovery, next-room restart and browser assets.
